data.title: Gold Rebounds Above $3,600 As CEO Nvidia Returns, Markets Trim Fed Hike
data.description:
Gold price (XAU/USD) rebounds from a more than one-year low to around $3,635 during the early Asian session on Tuesday. The precious metal edges higher as traders buy the dip. Market participants await upcoming US inflation data for further clues on the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) interest-rate trajectory.

The yellow metal rises after reports that Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia Corp.'s (NVDA) chief executive officer. Furthermore, signs of retail dip-buying have already emerged, supporting gold prices. In China, shops in Shenzhen’s Shuibei market, the epicenter of the country’s retail gold trade, were packed with people seeking to purchase jewelry, according to Song Jiangzhen, a researcher at Guangzhou Southern Gold Market Academy.

While traders continue to expect a 25-basis-point Fed rate hike in December, they have priced out the probability of a larger 50-basis-point increase, according to CME's FedWatch Tool. Higher rates are typically negative for gold, which doesn’t pay interest.

Traders brace for the US October Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Index, the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, due on Wednesday. This report could provide some hints about the likelihood of further rate hikes. Any signs of hotter inflation in the US could lift the US Dollar (USD) and exert some selling pressure on the USD-denominated commodity price.

Gold steadies but TD Securities warns market remains fragile as ETF outflows build

According to TD Securities, gold is "finally finding some respite" as the recent wave of selling shows signs of abating. The bank notes that "the pace of gold selling has finally eased somewhat, but the market remains fairly fragile with global ETF positions now showing signs of more material outflow." In their view, this does not signal "the total capitulation of gold's bullish outlook," but "rather remains more of a flow issue as global markets force a repricing of the Fed hike path." TD Securities argues that these developments "ultimately reinforce the gold market's fear of equity weakness, spiraling interest expense, stagflation, and fiscal dominance, which we believe will remain core longer-term upside drivers for the yellow metal."

Williams keeps hawkish bias as inflation seen above target for longer

Fed’s Williams delivered a speech that is broadly in line with the established baseline, with the FXS Speechtracker score at 6.2/10 matching the historical average and signaling a steady hawkish tone. Emphasis that the U.S. central bank “still has work to do” to return inflation to 2% and projections of 3.5% inflation at end-2026, only reaching target in 2028, underscore a higher-for-longer policy stance despite a resilient economy and stable job market. Acknowledgment that inflation risks are skewed to the upside, even as Williams does not see price pressures broadening much, keeps the bias tilted toward further or prolonged restraint rather than imminent easing, a backdrop typically supportive of the Dollar on rate expectations.

The FXS Fed Sentiment Index rose by 0.35 points to 152.49, reinforcing that the speech sits firmly in hawkish territory according to FXS Speechtracker metrics. With the index far above the 100 neutral line, markets are likely to interpret Williams’ remarks as validating elevated policy rates for an extended period, a configuration that can underpin the Dollar against lower-yielding peers.

Technical Analysis: Gold keeps a bearish vibe under the 100-day SMA

In the daily chart, XAU/USD remains under clear downside pressure, holding below the 20-day Bollinger simple moving average and the 100-day simple moving average (SMA), which both act as overhead resistance and suggest rallies are likely to be sold into. The 14-day Relative Strength Index sits just above the oversold threshold around 33, hinting at weak but not exhausted bearish momentum as price consolidates near recent lows.

On the downside, immediate support aligns with the lower Bollinger Band near $3,585, where a break would expose further weakness and keep the broader bearish bias intact. On the topside, a daily close back above the mid-Bollinger band around $3,915 would be the first sign of easing selling pressure, while the 100-day SMA at $4,175 and the upper band near $4,245 form a higher resistance cluster that would need to be reclaimed to challenge the prevailing downtrend.

data.title: CrowdStrike And Zscaler Building A Formidable AI Moat
data.description:
On November 23, 2026, markets received confirmation of a deal that had been rumored for days: CrowdStrike (CRWD) is acquiring Zscaler (ZS) in an all-stock deal worth nearly $43.9 billion.

Big acquisitions always raise eyebrows among investors, but CrowdStrike has an exceptional track record of integrating acquisitions, and the Zscaler deal makes a lot of strategic sense.

CrowdStrike and Zscaler together will be arguably the strongest cybersecurity company in the world, with over 10 billion in ARR (Annual Recurring Revenue) and covering all security needs with top-level AI capabilities.

The Deal

Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 shares of CrowdStrike common stock for each Zscaler share under this agreement. Based on current market prices, that means nearly $260.41 per Zscaler share, valuing the company at approximately $43.9 billion.

That implied price represents a roughly 34% premium to Zscaler’s Friday closing price of $194.82. Once the deal closes, existing CrowdStrike shareholders will own approximately 84.1% of the combined company, while Zscaler shareholders will own 15.9%.

Both boards unanimously approved the deal. Critically, Jay Chaudhry and his affiliates, who hold roughly 34% of Zscaler’s outstanding shares, signed binding voting agreements supporting the transaction.

Rather than walking away with a large wire transfer, Chaudhry is rolling his fortune into CrowdStrike equity, continuing to lead the Zscaler business post-close, and taking a seat on CrowdStrike’s Board of Directors.

Both companies expect the transaction to close in the second half of CrowdStrike’s fiscal year 2028 (which runs from August 2027 through January 2028), pending Zscaler shareholder sign-off and global regulatory clearances.

Financing And Valuation

Investors naturally dislike dilution, which explains why CrowdStrike stock is initially down by 8% after the announcement, as the share count will increase roughly 18% after this deal. However, the capital allocation considerations make a lot of sense on deeper review.

CrowdStrike stock was relatively expensive as the deal was being negotiated. The stock price is booming due to spectacular growth and profitability metrics, with a market capitalization near $216 billion. CrowdStrike stock is up nearly 80% year-to-date, a remarkable outperformance in a tough market for tech stocks.

Zscaler, on the other hand, had been unfairly beaten up, down more than 16% year-to-date, due to market panic over whether AI coding tools would let enterprises cheaply clone traditional SaaS products.

In terms of EV-to-revenue ratio, CrowdStrike stock is aggressively valued at almost 43 times revenue, while Zscaler trades at a much cheaper 9 times revenue.

Data by YCharts

When your currency (CrowdStrike stock) trades at a big premium and a premier strategic asset sits in the penalty box, using equity to lock in a transformational acquisition is textbook corporate finance. You are trading expensive shares for undervalued, mission-critical infrastructure.

Importantly, this acquisition is being done from a position of strength, as CrowdStrike has just reported excellent numbers for the third quarter of fiscal year 2027, which is the period ended on October 31, 2026 for the company. Both sales and earnings exceeded expectations during the quarter, and fundamental indicators keep moving in the right direction.

Total revenue reached $1.58 billion, growing 28.5% versus the same quarter in the prior year. Net new ARR reached a record $419 million, an increase of 58% and surpassing the company's guidance by more than $70 million. In a display of confidence, management raised the new ARR guidance by 790 basis points, now expecting 45% year-over-year growth for the full year.

Operating profit margin came in at 26% of revenue, with free cash flow margin above 30%. This combination of vigorous growth and strong profitability at scale is quite remarkable.

Management sees AI agents as the next major frontier in cybersecurity, as these agents are always on and can launch increasingly sophisticated attacks at unprecedented speed. Falcon Guardian, which secures and manages AI agents, is now CrowdStrike's fastest-growing product, recently surpassing $100 million in ARR in less than a year.

Revenue And Cost Synergies

Management estimates this deal could create $1 billion in annualized revenue run-rate synergies in the first 30 months and $500 million in cost savings over the next 18 to 24 months after close. Analysts are always skeptical of these projections, and for good reason, because management teams almost always overpromise and underestimate integration headaches. With this in mind, let's take a look at the numbers behind this guidance.

The press release cites 8,000 non-overlapping Zscaler customers. If we assume CrowdStrike can cross-sell Falcon to just 15% of them, that would bring 1,200 enterprise accounts at an average annual contract value (ACV) of $400,000; that alone would generate $480 million in new ARR.

CrowdStrike also has tens of thousands of customers, including massive Fortune 1000 accounts already spending millions on Falcon Flex, that do not yet use Zscaler. Converting just 600 to 800 of those large Falcon Flex accounts onto Zscaler Zero Trust SASE and AI Protect at an average ACV of $700,000 yields another $420 million to $560 million in ARR.

We can also consider deeper upsells to the more than 2,000 shared customers who now have a powerful financial and operational incentive to consolidate onto Falcon Next-Gen SIEM (streaming Zscaler logs natively at a lower ingestion cost than Splunk or Sentinel).

Based on these numbers, $1 billion in run-rate revenue synergies actually looks achievable, even slightly conservative, provided sales execution stays consistent and disciplined.

On the cost side, CrowdStrike and Zscaler will operate on a combined annual operating expense base well north of $7 billion by 2028-2029. Finding $500 million in run-rate savings represents roughly 6% to 7% of combined operating expenses, which is well within standard benchmarks for mergers in this sector.

Without touching R&D, there is a lot of room to eliminate redundant G&A in areas like audit, legal, IR, finance, and real estate overhead. The go-to-market strategy can also drive efficiencies, since both companies have large enterprise sales forces and marketing budgets targeting the same CISOs at the same conferences. I would also expect some cost savings in areas like cloud infrastructure due to scale and negotiating power after the merger.

Risk Considerations

At $43.9 billion, this is one of the largest software acquisitions in history. Given the deal's size, I think antitrust enforcers at the U.S. Department of Justice, the FTC, the European Commission, and the UK’s CMA may be paying close attention.

The bull case for approval is that CrowdStrike and Zscaler barely compete. Endpoint protection and inline Zero Trust network security are classic complementary markets.

Regulators already set a strong 2026 precedent by clearing Google’s (GOOG) (GOOGL) $32 billion Wiz deal and Palo Alto’s (PANW) $25 billion CyberArk deal. Besides, CrowdStrike can argue it needs this combination to compete effectively against even larger rivals like Palo Alto Networks, Alphabet, and Microsoft (MSFT).

We can expect intense regulatory scrutiny over bundling and tying. To ease these concerns, CrowdStrike may need to make formal interoperability commitments, such as keeping Zscaler’s open APIs working cleanly with Microsoft Defender and SentinelOne, just as Google promised Wiz would remain multicloud. This sounds doable and reasonable.

Deal limbo is another risk. Until the deal closes, CrowdStrike and Zscaler must legally operate as completely independent competitors. They cannot merge sales teams, cannot bundle Falcon Flex + Z-Flex on a single contract, and cannot share confidential pricing. In enterprise software, a 14-month limbo window is prime hunting season for rivals, and the competition will aggressively target Zscaler’s pipeline during 2027.

The good part is that the strategic partnership between CrowdStrike and Zscaler was already in place before the announcement. This means CrowdStrike and Zscaler can legally continue building and marketing their already-announced integrations through the regulatory waiting period.

George Kurtz and Jay Chaudhry are two of the most driven, intensely competitive founder-CEOs in Silicon Valley history. Both built category-defining titans from scratch, and they have strong views on architecture and go-to-market execution.

In practice, integrating a proud former standalone CEO into a subsidiary leadership role almost always creates cultural friction. Avoiding a cultural split between sales and engineering teams will require genuine executive diplomacy from both leaders, and no one can know in advance how this subtle, complex process will go.

Widening The Moat

The widening of the moat is perhaps the most important advantage in this deal. Revenue growth can be bought temporarily; economic moats, on the other hand, are what let a company compound free cash flow at high returns on capital for ten or twenty years without getting commoditized. This is essentially the most important consideration for long-term investors in CrowdStrike.

The data moat is absolutely crucial. In the AI era, foundation models are rapidly commoditizing. Open-weight models and frontier APIs are available to everyone. Proprietary, real-time, labeled operational data is the only AI moat that lasts, and CrowdStrike has just assembled a formidable data engine.

Falcon already generates trillions of security events every day from endpoints, identities, browsers, and cloud workloads worldwide. Zscaler’s Zero Trust Exchange processes more than 750 billion inline network transactions every single day across over 200 global locations.

When SafeMind correlates trillions of endpoint/identity signals with 750 billion daily inline network transactions in real time, it learns adversary patterns that single-domain competitors literally can't see. Better data trains smarter models; smarter models produce superior results. At the same time, higher efficacy attracts more enterprise customers, and more customers generate even more valuable data. That is a classic self-reinforcing AI data flywheel.

Switching costs will add another layer of competitive strength. CrowdStrike and Zscaler already had strong moats in this area before the deal, and they will only get stronger now.

Ripping out CrowdStrike Falcon across 100,000 endpoints, hundreds of cloud clusters, identity directories, and a Next-Gen SIEM packed with years of compliance logs is a multi-quarter operational nightmare and a very risky process to consider undertaking.

Replacing Zscaler’s Zero Trust Exchange, which sits directly in the live traffic path of every employee, branch office, and private application across 185+ countries, is even scarier and more complicated. It means that you are effectively rerouting the corporate nervous system while the patient is awake.

If we consider both companies together, once an enterprise runs its endpoints, identities, browser security, cloud workloads, inline Zero Trust network, and SOC automation on a single unified CRWD+ZS control plane, the switching cost becomes gigantic.

It will be incredibly hard to convince C-level management to take on millions of dollars in migration risk and the associated processes. This gigantic switching cost not only protects the business, but it also creates more opportunities for cross-selling in years to come. If you are not leaving CRWD+ZS, you will probably buy more from them in the future.

The Big Picture

Although big mergers are usually disliked for very good reasons, it is crucial to identify the exceptions to the rule. In this case, CrowdStrike is using its aggressively valued shares to buy a much cheaper business with remarkable strategic advantages. Together, the two companies are building a phenomenal data moat, perhaps the most crucial driver of success in the age of AI.

data.title: BofA Says Buy These 3 Stocks Heading Into 2027
data.description:
Bank of America analysts see several reasons to load up on Disney (DIS), Caterpillar (CAT), and Medtronic (MDT) shares as 2026 draws to a close.

DIS is entering a new fiscal year after a stronger-than-expected quarter; MDT has an investor event coming up that could clarify its earnings outlook, and CAT may earn more in the next “industrial downturn” than it did in past slumps.

The three names carry Buy ratings at BofA heading into 2027.

Why is BofA bullish on Disney stock?

Disney’s Q4 sales, operating income and earnings per share (EPS) all topped BofA analyst Jessica Reif Ehrlich’s expectations.

Adjusted EPS rose 59% to $1.77, helped by an extra week in the quarter. Disney estimates it would have earned $1.59 a share on the same adjusted basis without that benefit, still up 43% from a year earlier.

Management reiterated its forecast for double-digit adjusted EPS growth in fiscal 2027.

For investors, streaming margins offer a way to track that outlook. Disney’s subscription streaming business earned an 11.5% operating margin in fiscal 2026.

Further gains would show how much of the revenue growth Disney can turn into profit while continuing to invest in programming. DIS shares pay a dividend yield of 1.48% as well.

Why is BofA bullish on Medtronic stock?

Medtronic reports fiscal Q2 earnings on November 24, but BofA analyst Travis Steed sees a potential catalyst at the company’s Dec. 10–11 investor event.

He expects Medtronic to update its full-year outlook to exclude the diabetes business and explain how the revised numbers compare with its previous guidance.

That would give investors a cleaner starting point for estimating what Medtronic can earn as it separates MiniMed. Steed sees pre-pandemic gross margins as a longer-term goal and expects the plan to fall short of that level.

What could move MDT stock is a credible path to higher earnings per share while preserving room to invest in new devices. Note that Medtronic currently pays a dividend yield of 2.88%.

Why is BofA bullish on Caterpillar stock?

BofA’s Caterpillar thesis hinges on what the equipment maker can earn when demand cools. The bank expects profits at the bottom of the next cycle to hold above levels seen in past downturns.

Power equipment helps explain that view. Data center operators need generators, giving Caterpillar another source of orders alongside its traditional construction and mining customers.

Third-quarter sales climbed 17% to $20.7 billion, and the backlog reached a record $78.1 billion.

Caterpillar held its full-year sales growth forecast steady amid cost pressures.

Heading into 2027, the question is how quickly the company can deliver those orders and how much profit it keeps as it adds capacity.

CAT shares currently pay a dividend yield of 1.28%.

data.title: Retatrutide, CagriSema, Tesofensine And BAM15: The Next Weight Loss Drugs After Ozempic
data.description:
Among the weight loss drugs that will follow Ozempic, the race for the biggest number on the scale is over. On May 21, Eli Lilly reported that retatrutide, its weekly triple-hormone injection, cut body weight by 28.3% on average after 80 weeks at the top dose, and that 45.3% of patients on that dose lost at least 30% of their weight. Five months earlier, in a trial in people with knee osteoarthritis, 18.2% of patients on the top dose had stopped treatment because of side effects, against 4.0% on placebo, and Lilly wrote that some of those stops were for "perceived excessive weight loss". When patients quit a drug because it works too well, efficacy has stopped being what separates the winners.

My thesis, in one paragraph: retatrutide has won the efficacy race, and the stock market knows it. Lilly's shares are up 26% over the past year and Novo Nordisk's US-listed shares are down 16%. The next phase of the obesity market will be decided by three things that a headline weight-loss number hides: how much of the weight lost is fat and how much is muscle, how many patients can stay on the drug, and what insurers and governments will pay. On those three counts the board is more open than share prices suggest. Novo's CagriSema, written off after it lost to Lilly's tirzepatide in February, now faces a low bar in its next trial, and the options market does not price that readout as a special event. Two other molecules, tesofensine and BAM15, have no coverage from any major bank. Both deserve a sourced public file, if only to show why one is a small regulatory option for a Stockholm-listed biotech and the other cannot be an investment today.

The four molecules at a glance

  • Retatrutide (Eli Lilly LLY). A weekly injection that mimics three gut and pancreas hormones: GLP-1 and GIP cut appetite, glucagon raises energy use and the burning of liver fat. Best data: 28.3% weight loss at 80 weeks (TRIUMPH-1). Next: a US filing planned for the first quarter of 2027.

  • CagriSema (Novo Nordisk NVO). A weekly injection of semaglutide, the drug in Ozempic and Wegovy, plus cagrilintide, a long-acting version of amylin, a hormone that signals fullness. Best data: 23.0% at 84 weeks, short of tirzepatide's 25.5% (REDEFINE 4). Next: an FDA decision expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, then REDEFINE 11 results in the first half of 2027.

  • Tesofensine (Saniona; Medix holds Mexico and Argentina). A daily pill that keeps three brain messengers (serotonin, noradrenaline, dopamine) active for longer, which cuts appetite. Best data: about 10% average weight loss at 24 weeks in Medix's phase 3 in Mexico (the company did not say whether net of placebo), never published in full. Next: a decision by COFEPRIS, Mexico's drug regulator, pending since the February 2025 resubmission.

  • BAM15 (no listed owner; university patents licensed to private start-ups). Makes mitochondria, the cell's power plants, burn fuel as heat (a "mitochondrial uncoupler"). Best data: mice only. Next: no human trial registered.

A word on the numbers. Obesity trials report two averages. The first counts patients as if they had all stayed on the drug; the second counts everyone who was randomized, including those who stopped, and is lower: 25.0% for retatrutide's top dose in TRIUMPH-1. Comparisons across trials are rough, because the patients, the durations and the doses differ. The only clean comparisons are head-to-head trials, and there are few of them.

Retatrutide: the race is won, the bill comes next

The evidence is broad. In TRIUMPH-1 (2,339 adults without diabetes who had obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition), weight fell 19.0%, 25.9% and 28.3% at the 4 mg, 9 mg and 12 mg doses after 80 weeks, against 2.2% on placebo. In an extension to 104 weeks, open only to patients with a body mass index of 35 or more who had completed the first 80 weeks and tolerated their dose, the 12 mg arm reached 30.3%. People with type 2 diabetes lost about 20% of their weight (20.8% at 12 mg in TRIUMPH-2) and, in a head-to-head trial against Ozempic's highest dose, it cut blood sugar more (HbA1c, the three-month average of blood sugar, fell 2.2 points against 1.8) and weight twice as much (20.9% against 9.4%). In knee osteoarthritis (TRIUMPH-4), weight fell 28.7% at 68 weeks and knee pain scores dropped by about three quarters, against 40% on placebo, a percentage Lilly computed after the fact.

The bill is just as clear. At 12 mg in TRIUMPH-1, 42.4% of patients had nausea (14.8% on placebo), 25.3% vomited (4.8%), and 12.5% reported dysesthesia, an unpleasant or abnormal skin sensation such as tingling (0.9%). 11.3% stopped because of side effects, against 4.9% on placebo. In TRIUMPH-4 that share reached 18.2%, and Lilly said the stops were "highly correlated with baseline BMI": among patients with a body mass index of 35 or more, 12.1% stopped at 12 mg, so leaner patients quit more often. Against Ozempic in diabetes, 7.9% stopped on retatrutide 12 mg, against 2.7%. Retatrutide also raised heart rate in its phase 2 trial, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2023, with a peak around week 24 and a decline after. Lilly's phase 3 releases report lower blood pressure (systolic pressure fell 14.0 mmHg at the top dose in TRIUMPH-4, a figure Lilly flags as not adjusted for multiple testing) and better blood fats, but give no heart-rate figures. The FDA review should.

The chart is the whole thesis. Going from 9 mg to 12 mg adds 2.4 points of weight loss in TRIUMPH-1 and 2.3 points in TRIUMPH-4, and raises the share of patients who stop by 4.4 and 6.0 points. Beyond about 25%, each extra point of efficacy costs tolerability. That is why I expect retatrutide to become a drug for severe obesity, for men and for people with type 2 diabetes (in those last two groups, Lilly's management says it is the first agent to exceed 20% weight loss), while tirzepatide and cheaper options cover the rest. Bloomberg Intelligence makes the same point on price: used mainly by specialists for severe obesity if priced above Zepbound, or with lower doses priced alongside Zepbound and a premium for the higher ones.

Lilly plans to file in the United States in the first quarter of 2027, which points to a decision around early 2028. A head-to-head trial against tirzepatide, TRIUMPH-5 (about 800 adults, 80 weeks), is under way. Lilly has given no date, but the registry entry lists November 2026 for the last primary measurement, so results could come in the first half of 2027, before the options below expire. Its result matters more to my thesis than any other: a wide gap with similar tolerability would prove that efficacy still decides.

The market has priced most of this. Lilly closed at $1,347.11 on Friday, for a market value of $1.27 trillion, after a 69.6% rise from its lowest close of the past year, on April 29, to its highest, $1,443.50 on November 13. Part of that premium has little to do with any single trial: in If the AI Trade Breaks, Where Do You Hide? on November 19, health care rose 0.47% on average, and was up 61% of the time, on the 31 sessions of 2026 when chip stocks lost 3% or more. Lilly is the largest health care stock in that refuge.

Trade on Lilly (one branch). If retatrutide's tolerability and price become the story, the downside comes from a stock priced for the good outcome. A defined-risk way to express it is a put spread (buying a put and selling a lower one to cap the cost) through the filing, the likely TRIUMPH-5 readout and the first-quarter results: buy the June 17, 2027 $1,300 put and sell the $1,100 put. Priced on my Bloomberg on Sunday, November 22, at 3:13 p.m. Paris time, from Friday's closing quotes, it costs $67.58 per share at mid-market (the average of bid and ask), or $78.90 when buying at the offer and selling at the bid. It breaks even at $1,232.42, 8.5% below Friday's close, and pays its maximum of $200, about 3 times its cost, at or below $1,100. The options expire on Thursday, June 17, because Friday, June 18, 2027 is the Juneteenth market holiday. Implied volatility, the yearly swing priced into options, sits between about 35% and 39% on Lilly from December to June, highest on the February and March expiries, which include fourth-quarter results expected on February 4.

CagriSema: priced for failure, which makes the next readout interesting

On February 23, Novo reported that CagriSema produced 23.0% weight loss at 84 weeks against 25.5% for tirzepatide in REDEFINE 4, missing its goal of showing it was not worse. Novo's US-listed shares fell 16.4% that day. They are now 41% below their January 26 high, and analysts followed: Barclays cut its risk-adjusted peak-sales estimate from $12 billion to $2 billion, and Bloomberg Intelligence, which had expected $7 billion of obesity sales by 2030 before the trial, notes that consensus estimates for CagriSema's contribution over 2026 to 2030 have nearly halved.

The drug is still on track. Novo announced its FDA filing on December 18, 2025, at the 2.4 mg/2.4 mg dose, and expects a decision in the fourth quarter of 2026. In September, a lower dose (1.0 mg/1.0 mg) beat tirzepatide 5 mg in people with type 2 diabetes (12.4% against 9.1% at 60 weeks in REIMAGINE 5) and, in adults with overweight or obesity, produced 21.0% weight loss against 2.0% on placebo at 68 weeks in REDEFINE 9. The trial that matters is REDEFINE 11: about 600 people, 80 weeks, against placebo, with what analysts describe as a stricter protocol for bringing patients who had to lower their dose back up to the full dose. The registry entry that matches it lists March 2027 for the last primary measurement, so results should come in the first half of 2027. A 7,000-patient cardiovascular outcomes trial, REDEFINE 3, follows, with primary completion estimated for September 2027.

The bar is low. Before its first phase 3 results, in December 2024, Novo had said it expected about 25% weight loss. A result in that zone in REDEFINE 11, with fewer patients stopping, would put CagriSema back in the tirzepatide conversation, as a better-tolerated option built on the best-known molecule in the class. A result near REDEFINE 1's 22.7% would change little, and that is roughly what the share price already assumes. The options market agrees: on Novo's US-listed shares, at-the-money implied volatility is 36.7% for June 2027, the expiry that should cover REDEFINE 11, below the 39.1% of March 2027, which spans full-year results on February 3. Nobody is paying up for the readout. My view: CagriSema will reach the market as a second-tier drug, but the stock's reaction to REDEFINE 11 is asymmetric, because expectations are close to zero.

Trades on Novo (one per branch). Both are priced on my Bloomberg on Sunday, November 22, at 3:10 p.m. Paris time, from Friday's closing quotes, for options expiring on Thursday, June 17, 2027. Novo's US-listed shares closed at $37.82.

  • If REDEFINE 11 surprises: buy the $40 call and sell the $50 call, for $2.35 per share at mid-market ($2.56 at market), $235 per contract of 100 shares. It breaks even above $42.35, 12% above Friday's close, and pays its maximum of $10.00, 4.3 times its cost, at or above $50, a level the shares last closed above on July 30 ($51.61).

  • If it disappoints or the FDA delays: buy the $35 put and sell the $27.50 put, for $2.09 per share at mid-market ($2.28 at market). It breaks even below $32.91, 13% under Friday's close, and pays its maximum of $7.50, 3.6 times its cost, at or below $27.50.

The call spread costs a little more than the put spread ($2.35 against $2.09), breaks even after a slightly smaller move (12% against 13%) and pays a third more at most ($10.00 against $7.50). That is the asymmetry: the market charges about the same for both branches while the bad news is already in the price. I prefer the call spread; the put spread is the hedge for holders of the shares.

Tesofensine: a cheap pill for Mexico, and a small option for Saniona

Tesofensine is the oldest idea of the four. The Danish company NeuroSearch developed it for Parkinson's and Alzheimer's disease; it failed there, but patients lost weight. It is a daily pill that blocks the reuptake of three brain messengers, noradrenaline, dopamine and serotonin, which cuts appetite. In a 24-week phase 2 trial in Denmark, published in The Lancet in 2008, patients lost 4.5%, 9.2% and 10.6% more weight than on placebo (2.0%) at 0.25 mg, 0.5 mg and 1.0 mg, and heart rate rose by 7.4 beats per minute at 0.5 mg. Two caveats belong next to those numbers. In 2013 The Lancet attached an expression of concern to the paper, after the Danish medicines agency found problems at two of the five trial sites, including side effects that were under-recorded. And the phase 3 program planned around 2010, 5,000 to 7,000 patients with a cardiovascular study, never ran. NeuroSearch handed the drug in 2014, without any upfront payment, to Saniona, a small biotech listed in Stockholm and based near Copenhagen.

Saniona licensed Mexico and Argentina to the Mexican drugmaker Medix in 2016. Medix's phase 3 trial in Mexico (372 patients, 24 weeks, 0.25 mg and 0.5 mg against placebo) reported "ten per cent average weight loss" in December 2018, with more than half of patients losing over 10%, unchanged blood pressure and a small rise in heart rate. The full results have never appeared in a journal. Medix filed with COFEPRIS, Mexico's drug regulator, at the end of 2019. A technical committee gave a favorable but non-binding opinion in February 2023, approval was withheld in November 2024, Medix resubmitted in February 2025, and Saniona's reports in 2026 describe the file as "under review", with no date. Tesomet, a combination with the beta-blocker metoprolol for rare forms of obesity, was paused in March 2022 for lack of funding and is offered for partnering.

The economics are small. Medix would owe Saniona up to $2.0 million of regulatory milestones, none paid by the end of 2025, and royalties in the low double digits on sales in its two countries. Saniona is worth SEK 1.55 billion, down 47% this year, held SEK 486 million of cash at the end of June, and earns most of its deal income from ion-channel programs partnered with Jazz (JAZZ) and Acadia (ACAD). No bank covers it: on my Bloomberg, the only sources are an independent research firm that does not rate the stock, a paid corporate research note from 2025 and a quantitative score.

The price argument is weakening as well. Semaglutide's patents expired around March 20, 2026 in India, China, Brazil and Mexico, and generic versions have been approved in India, Brazil and Canada. According to the Mexican press, none had been approved in Mexico by mid-November, and Medix itself plans a cheaper semaglutide biosimilar with Biocon for 2027. A daily pill with a heart-rate signal would compete with cheap weekly semaglutide sold by the same partner.

My view: a COFEPRIS approval would be a small regulatory option for Saniona, with milestones capped at $2 million and royalties on Mexican and Argentine sales only, and no change for the global market. Watch heart rate and blood pressure in any published data, and the full phase 3 results, which have never been released.

BAM15: the best science, and why it is not an investment

BAM15 attacks the problem from the other end. Incretin drugs such as semaglutide make people eat less. BAM15 makes cells waste energy. It lets protons leak across the inner membrane of the mitochondria, so the cell burns more fuel for the same output and the difference leaves the body as heat. Biologists call this uncoupling.

The molecule was found in a screen at the University of Virginia, in Kyle Hoehn's lab with the chemist Webster Santos of Virginia Tech, and described in 2013. Two mouse studies made it famous in 2020. In Nature Communications, obese mice given BAM15 in their food for five weeks weighed 15% less than untreated mice eating the same amount; almost all the difference was fat, lean mass did not change and body temperature did not rise. In EMBO Molecular Medicine, a second team found that BAM15 kept mice on a fatty diet from gaining weight, without any fall in food intake. That study also adds a caveat that the enthusiasts skip: compared with a diet that produced the same weight loss, BAM15 burned more fat, but lean mass still ended below that of untreated mice.

None of this has been tested in a human trial. ClinicalTrials.gov lists no trial of BAM15, and its inventors said in 2020 that this exact molecule may not work in people; in mice its half-life is only a few hours, and they said they had made several hundred analogues. The patents I could find are held by the University of Virginia's patent foundation and by Virginia Tech, and conflict-of-interest statements published in 2020 and 2024 mention licences to two private start-ups, Continuum Biosciences and Uncoupler Biosciences. No listed company owns BAM15, which is why no bank covers it.

The class has a history. 2,4-dinitrophenol (DNP), an uncoupler sold as a diet pill in the 1930s after work at Stanford, has a safety margin that an FDA scientist described as "razor thin": the dose that burns fat is close to the dose that overheats the body. 62 deaths had been published by 2011, and 16.9% of the DNP poisonings reported to UK poison services from 2007 to 2018 were fatal. DNP is still sold online to bodybuilders, and a peer-reviewed study published in February 2026 looked at how bodybuilding forums and YouTube now present BAM15 as "the new DNP". I will say it plainly: nobody should take BAM15, or any uncoupler, outside a clinical trial.

The idea has reached the clinic in forms designed to be safer. Rivus Pharmaceuticals' HU6 is a pill that the liver converts into DNP in a controlled way. In patients with obesity and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction it cut weight by 2.86 kg more than placebo over 19 weeks, almost all of it fat (JAMA Cardiology, 2025), and a larger phase 2 trial in fatty liver disease is expected to report in mid-2027, according to Rivus. OrsoBio's TLC-6740, a liver-targeted uncoupler, added 4.5 points of weight loss to a low dose of tirzepatide over 24 weeks (13.3% against 8.8%) in a 55-person trial reported by the company in December 2025.

My view: BAM15 is the most interesting science of the four, because it burns fat without touching appetite and, in mice, mostly spares muscle. It is not an investable asset today: no human trial, no listed owner, and a class whose safety margin has to be proven molecule by molecule. The closest thing to an investable version of the idea, for now, is liver-targeted uncouplers combined with incretins, and they sit in private companies.

What would prove me wrong

  • Retatrutide. TRIUMPH-5 shows a wide gap over tirzepatide with similar rates of stopping, or the FDA label is clean on heart rate and the drug launches near Zepbound's price. Efficacy would then still decide, and Lilly's premium would be deserved.

  • CagriSema. The FDA delays or rejects the filing, or REDEFINE 11 comes in below REDEFINE 1 with as many patients stopping. Pricing pressure on Wegovy could also weigh more on the shares than any trial result.

  • Tesofensine. COFEPRIS approves it, Medix prices it well below generic semaglutide and Saniona reports real royalties, or a partner takes it into trials in the United States or Europe.

  • BAM15. An analogue enters a registered human trial with a clean safety profile, or a listed company buys the rights. It would then become investable, and I would revisit it.

The calendar

  • November 26, 2026. Saniona third-quarter report.

  • Q4 2026. FDA decision on CagriSema (Novo's guidance; no public date).

  • February 3, 2027. Novo Nordisk full-year results (date confirmed).

  • February 4, 2027. Eli Lilly fourth-quarter results (expected date).

  • February 25, 2027. Saniona year-end report.

  • Q1 2027. Retatrutide US filing (Lilly's plan).

  • First half of 2027. REDEFINE 11 results (registry primary completion March 2027).

  • First half of 2027. TRIUMPH-5 results, retatrutide against tirzepatide (registry primary completion November 2026; no date from Lilly).

  • June 17, 2027. Expiry of the option trades above.

  • Mid-2027. Phase 2 results of Rivus's HU6 in fatty liver disease.

  • September 2027. REDEFINE 3 cardiovascular trial, estimated primary completion.

  • Early 2028. Possible US approval of retatrutide.

  • No date. COFEPRIS decision on tesofensine in Mexico.

What comes next for me. I will follow two numbers: the share of patients who stop each new drug, and the price at which it launches. Weight loss has had its race. The next one is about who can stay on treatment, and at what cost.

data.title: New Nvidia CEO Is The Old One: Huang Returns, NVDA Soars 35% And Bitcoin Follows
data.description:
In the end, Nvidia’s board backed down and reinstated Jensen Huang as the “new” Nvidia (NVDA) CEO. The announcement triggered a broad market rebound, sending stocks higher and adding trillions in market value. But skepticism remains high, particularly across the crypto market, where investors are still waiting for signs of a sustained recovery.

Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive on Monday, November 23, 11 days after he resigned, and the stock exploded. The new Nvidia CEO is the old one, and investors cheered. Shares jumped from about $136 to as high as $169 in pre-market trading after the 8:55 a.m. ET announcement.

That peak was 35% above Friday’s close of $125.53. The stock opened near $163 and traded around $160 shortly after, still up 27%. Crypto went along for the ride. Bitcoin (BTC.X) rose as much as 5% to about $64,100, and Ethereum (ETH-X) as much as 7%.

The reversal came a day after President Donald Trump urged the board to bring Huang back. “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang,” Trump wrote on Truth Social on Sunday.

So how much of the scandal sell-off has Nvidia won back, and what comes next?

New Nvidia CEO: The Board Reverses Itself in Six Days

Nvidia’s board “voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang” after meetings with him, it said in its announcement. It said it was satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead.”

It is a sharp turn. On November 17, chair Harvey Jones said the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and had hired a search firm for a new Nvidia CEO.

The government helped change that. The board said it heard from “senior levels of the United States government” before deciding. Based on that input, it is confident Huang’s return “poses no national security risk.” Huang resigned on November 12 after admitting an affair with a woman US intelligence suspects of spying for China.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA,” Huang said. “I can’t wait to get back to work.”

Colette Kress, who ran the company as interim CEO, stays on as finance chief. The board’s independent investigation into the foreign intelligence effort will continue, and Nvidia said it will keep cooperating with government inquiries.

NVDA Won Back More Than Half of the Scandal Drop

To measure how much the new Nvidia CEO news repaired, we compared Monday’s price with Nvidia’s closes before and during the scandal.

Nvidia closed at $186.64 on November 6, the last session before Huang’s affair came out. By Friday it was down to $125.53, a loss of $61.11 a share. At $160, the stock has recovered 56% of that drop. At the $169 peak, it had won back 71%.

The peak took it above its close on November 12, the day Huang resigned ($166.19). Even at $160, the jump adds about $830 billion to Nvidia’s market value in a single morning.

The stock is still far from its highs. It sits 33% below its October 6 record close of $239.24, because it had already fallen 22% on AI spending worries before the scandal began.

Bitcoin’s move shows how closely crypto now trades with Nvidia. BTC jumped from about $61,100 to above $63,000 in the same minutes as NVDA, and crypto stocks such as Strategy (MSTR) also rose.

NVDA Price Analysis: $170 Is the Next Test

Nvidia stock trades around $160, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $186, and its 200-day EMA at $202.

  • Resistance: $170, the floor from November 2025 to March 2026. Above that, $185, where the stock stalled several times last winter.

  • Support: $150, the level Nvidia broke last week, now a floor to hold.

XYZ:NVDAUSD 1D chart. Source: Hyperliquid

What comes next depends on Washington more than the boardroom. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wants answers from Nvidia by November 25 on whether its chips reached China through shell companies. A reported SEC look at its accounting is still open. Huang is also due to testify to Congress in December.

With the new Nvidia CEO back in charge, those answers will decide whether the stock can hold above $150.

data.title: The Shopify 2.0 Playbook: Inside Rezolve AI’s Proprietary Tech Stack, Parabolic Growth, And The Roadmap To Profitability
data.description:
TM Editor's Note: This article discusses one or more penny stocks and/or microcaps. Such stocks are easily manipulated; do your own careful due diligence.

  • Rezolve AI is building the ecosystem & payment rails for Agentic Commerce

  • Top-Line Growth - H1 2026 revenue surged nearly 21-fold to $130.8M

  • Recurring revenue base of over 1,640 enterprise customers

  • $500M+ run rate target for EOY 2026

  • The Profitability Pivot targeted for H1 2027

  •  Approximately $60M in annualized cost savings

When Shopify (Nasdaq: SHOP) debuted a decade ago, Wall Street initially miscategorized it as just another web builder. They missed the forest for the trees because Shopify wasn't selling website templates; it was providing the fundamental operating system for independent digital commerce. After a decade of experience optimizing websites for the direct to consumer (DTC) experience brand, retailers are facing declining human interactions. Bot traffic is outpacing human traffic and represents 62% of all website traffic according to Cloudflare Radar and the gap is widening. What matters now is how a brand looks to an AI agent versus a human.    

Today, retail is undergoing its third major structural revolution. As consumer shopping habits migrate from static keyword search bars to conversational AI assistants and autonomous agentic workflows, Rezolve AI (Nasdaq: RZLV) is positioned as the infrastructure backbone  of this new paradigm.  The Rezolve ecosystem is AI-driven and free of AI hallucinations that have kept brands on the sidelines and is now capable of interfacing with this new era of ecommerce.

Understanding the AI Hallucination

Brands are ultimately built on the idea of trust.  This means that the Brands need to consistently deliver a quality product, at a reasonable price, that is reliable, and supports the customer with factually correct information. Any break in that consumer trust is capable of destroying the brand image.

For a real-world parallel of how an AI hallucination works, look back to the recent situation with White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia. She made national news after repeatedly describing herself as a lawyer and attorney in TV appearances, online bios, and corporate titles, despite the fact that she never passed the bar or ever practiced law in a US jurisdiction. While she did graduate from law school and could talk fluently on legal topics, she was in fact NOT a lawyer.  This tarnished her brand to the point that she only lasted 5 days in the press secretary position.  AIs don’t output uncertain text such as “I’m making a guess here, but I think …” Instead, the AI will fabricate facts with the same authoritative tone that is used for verified facts. 

While this seems like much to do about nothing, Brands are built on predictability, trust, and risk mitigation. The generative AI models are built on probabilistic next-token predictions, meaning they are designed to guess plausible-sounding text rather than verify facts. They are guessing the next token, not the truth.  For a Brand to utilize an AI model it must only speak the truth and there can be zero tolerance for a Brand error. There are a number of cases where Brands have deployed AI chatbots and later found out they are legally liable for the incorrect output. 

The Moffatt v. Air Canada Precedent 

The landmark case was Moffatt v. Air Canada, and it set a clear precedent that an enterprise cannot disown its AI hallucinations. In this case, a customer asked the airline’s website chatbot about bereavement fare discounts following a family loss. The chatbot hallucinated an inaccurate policy, promising the customer he could buy full-price tickets immediately and retroactively apply for a refund within 90 days. When Air Canada refused to honor the chatbot’s statement, claiming the accurate policy was located on a static webpage and that the chatbot was essentially a separate entity responsible for its own output, the British Columbia Civil Resolution Tribunal rejected the defense. 

When a brand deploys generative AI to interact directly with consumers, every output carries the full authority and liability of the company behind it. For platforms like Shopify and merchants relying on automated tools, Moffatt underscores why AI integrations require rigorous guardrails.  It only takes one probabilistic guess that can instantly turn into a legally binding brand promise.

Agentic Commerce Demands Absolute Accuracy   

Until Rezolve AI launched Brainpower, generative AI could not be reliably trusted by major enterprises. Fear of brand dilution, legal liability, and unpredictable hallucinations kept brands on the sidelines. While retailers have long known that in-store conversion rates dramatically outperform online channels because human sales associates can answer questions and guide the buyer in real time, digital channels suffer from static friction. 

Rezolve Commerce changes this paradigm by introducing an AI agent trained exclusively within the brand’s trusted ecosystem, completely eliminating the possibility of AI hallucinations. When a brand’s AI agent interacts with a consumer’s autonomous shopping agent, a truthful, friction-free exchange of information takes place, turning conversational intent into high-converting sales. 

Brainpower AI achieves this by grounding itself directly in real-time merchant catalog data, structured product feeds, and strict operational constraints. Instead of treating a product description as static text, Rezolve’s contextual engine reasons about the why behind every item in a catalog. The engine incorporates real-life scenarios, use cases, applications, sizing parameters, and local inventory levels. 

In the RZLV ecosystem, when a consumer or autonomous AI agent interacts with its brand client to go shopping, the system doesn't just guess. Instead, it checks real store data to give the consumer exact, helpful answers. By mixing friendly conversation with facts straight from the store's database, Rezolve makes sure its digital assistants can help shoppers pick out outfits and check out safely without making up rules or lying about the brand. In the new world of AI-driven shopping, this smart safety net gives brands a way to use AI without risking getting sued or ruining their good name. 

The Historic Parallel

Back when Shopify started, it fixed the headache of setting up online stores and payment accounts as shopping moved from physical malls to web browsers. Now, retail is going through a massive change where AI assistants shop and talk to each other for us. Because of this, it is starting to matter much more how a brand looks to an AI helper than to a human shopper. This is where Rezolve AI's commerce platform stands out. Just like Shopify became the secret engine powering millions of online brands, Rezolve AI is building the smart software and payment systems for this new age of AI shopping. 

We live in a world where AI agents versus humans are typing in words to a search bar for us and deciding which brands to show us.  Rezolve AI is the link between friendly chat-based searching and a smooth checkout for consumers. 

Financial Analysis: Parabolic Sales Growth Meets Operational Discipline

Valuation of early stage tech companies always draws intense scrutiny as did SHOP in the early days, but Rezolve AI’s financials show both a mix of explosive revenue growth along with a serious commitment to the bottom line. During the first half of 2026, the company reported $130.8 million in revenue, which is a staggering 1970% jump from the $6.3 million recorded in the first half of 2025, and nearly triples its total earnings for all of 2025. This momentum has fueled a massive expansion in its merchant ecosystem, growing to over 1640 enterprise customers up from about 950 at the end of 2025. It was able to onboard major global brands like H&M, Mango, Tommy Hilfiger/Clavin Klein (NYSE: PVH) and Coles to name a few. This establishes a robust base for annual recurring revenue (ARR) from highly reputable and stable companies, with several large cap companies listed as Trusted, such as BJ’s (NYSE: BJ - a competitor to Costco (Nasdaq: COST), and Fedex (NYSE: FDX)

Management recognized that rapid growth must be balanced with fiscal discipline. To achieve this, the company launched a strategic operating program aimed at cutting roughly $60 million in annual costs. By reining in discretionary marketing, streamlining professional services, and leaning on trusted partners like Tata Consultancy Services and Tech Mahindra to handle implementations, RZLV reduced its cash burn through the second half of 2026.  This clears the road toward positive adjusted EBITDA by the end of the first half of 2027. 

In addition to the growth and cost reductions is a share buyback. RZLV is a UK company which means they are required to report every 6 months and share buybacks are called capital reductions that need court approval. On October 6, 2026 they received court approval for a share repurchase of $300M. Management took the opportunity to say:

“We have consistently said that we believe the public market valuation of Rezolve Ai does not reflect the strength of our technology, the progress we have made commercially, or the scale of the opportunity ahead in AI-powered commerce.”   Daniel Wagner - Founder, Chairman & CEO | Rezolve AI

Share buybacks have a tendency to put a bid under the price and have the possibility of creating a new uptrend in the stock price.  But within this buyback announcement resonates a message of corporate confidence that they are executing on their plan, and they plan to deliver growth and earnings.  

Investment Summary

SHOP had a modest beginning and IPOed in 2015 at $1.90B market cap with $205.2M in revenue. This data point provides context for the parallel comparison with RZLV with $360M in EOY revenue and a market of $620M. Like Shopify, RZLV is solving a major market problem for Brands conducting ecommerce and is gaining incredible traction evident by their recurring revenue base.  They are creating a very sticky Brand ecosystem by unifying discovery (Rezolve Commerce), secure checkout (Rezolve Pay), customer loyalty (Rezolve Reward), and actionable merchant analytics (Rezolve Insights). Their solution provides an end-to-end infrastructure that global retailers desperately need to survive the shift to agentic commerce.  It's patented, it's gaining traction, the market is growing, and now the bottom line is now in sight.  

RZLV has taking a beating with the rest of the AI stocks but the Chart shows its way overdone. RZLV presents an asymmetric risk/reward setup for investors looking for the defining infrastructure play of the AI retail era. The company is in the rapid growth stage and the stock has taken a pause but during this pause a number of major milestones are brewing that could rerate the stock at the next earning report.  When ecommerce solutions like SHOP take root the platforms take off and never look back. The RZLV setup looks like SHOP 2.0.

data.title: Have Markets Hit Bottom?
data.description:
November has been an uncharacteristically bad month for financial markets. The rout has been primarily in the stock market, but the effect has been so massive that it’s influencing Forex. Across the board, stock markets have fallen, and traders have piled into safe-haven assets such as the dollar. Meanwhile, the demand for liquidity has left gold falling to levels not seen in more than a year.

However, as traders settle in on Monday, there are green shoots, with US futures broadly in the green. That’s significant because tech stocks, which are concentrated in the US, led the downside this month. After the Nasdaq fell into bear territory on an intraday basis last Friday, apparently some investors are hoping that the bottom is in, and it’s time to buy the dip. If they are right, what does that mean for Forex? Or will the trends in the currency markets continue into December?

A Short Week Could Help Revive the Market

US traders will be away from their desks for a holiday on Thursday and a shortened trading day on Friday. Typically, a notable holiday leads to lower liquidity, which increases volatility. However, in the current environment, that could provide some relief as it allows the generally more bullish retail traders to take a stronger role.

Analysts have noted that the recent drop across equities has been led by what is often called “smart money”. That is, the businesses themselves. Executives have the best insight into their sector’s performance and their own business, so when businesses sell stock or bonds, it is typically seen as a bad sign for the market. However, businesses are using the funds they are raising to fuel the massive AI build-out, which means the technical signs of distress might not align with the fundamentals. With institutional traders away for the holidays, there is likely to be less downward pressure.

How Will a Market Recovery Affect Forex?

If the bottom is in for tech stocks for now, and the market shifts into its traditional Santa Rally (December is the best-performing month of the year historically), then many recent trends in forex markets might reverse. Particularly, the strength of the dollar and the relatively weak performance of the Euro and Pound.

The Euro has come under sustained pressure over the last seven weeks as the dollar has rocketed higher amid increasing Fed hawkishness. Conversely, markets are worried about social unrest in France and what that might mean for public spending in the second-largest economy in Europe. That is the superficial read on the recent trends. However, the sell-off in US tech stocks has made them relatively undervalued, which could attract capital inflows and further support the dollar. In other words, a market rebound might not support the EURUSD.

What if There Isn’t a Rebound?

While it’s true that markets usually trend higher in December, that’s not always the case. In fact, it’s more common for a negative November to be followed by a negative December. Especially when the Fed is poised to keep raising rates.

In that scenario, the market is likely to keep piling into the dollar, which would likely come at the expense of commodity currencies like the NZD and AUD. The yen might manage to capture enough safe-haven trading to keep up with the dollar, particularly if the market still believes the BOJ will hike next month.

Ethereum price today: $1,720

  • Ethereum briefly rose above $1,800 after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as President and CEO.

  • The top altcoin erased most of the initial gains despite a strong rally across equities.

  • ETH was rejected near the $1,827 resistance after a quick spike.

Ethereum (ETH) failed to sustain its initial rebound on Monday despite a rally in technology stocks after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. BitMine added 7,819 ETH, while US spot ETH ETFs recorded another week of net outflows.

Huang’s return boosts market sentiment​

Ethereum briefly reclaimed $1,800 on Monday after Nvidia (NVDA) reinstated Jensen Huang as President and CEO.

"I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said in a press release on Monday.

Huang initially resigned from the company on November 12 following public disclosures and investigations into extramarital affairs, including one with an Nvidia executive and another with a woman US intelligence officials suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence.

Following his reinstatement, Nvidia stock popped over 30%, carrying AI-related equities alongside it. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) gained 14%, while the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 jumped 5% and 6.8%, respectively.

The gains briefly spilled into the crypto market, which jumped 4.6% before easing back. Ethereum fell back below $1,800 after a brief pop above that level.

The move sparked $157 million in ETH liquidations over the past 24 hours, including $108 million in short and $49 million in long liquidations, according to Coinglass data.

BitMine buys, but ETH ETF outflows continue

Meanwhile, Ethereum treasury firm BitMine Immersion Technologies (BMNR) continued expanding its treasury.

The firm scooped 7,819 ETH last week, expanding its stash of the top altcoin to 6.085 million ETH. That puts the company roughly 0.02% short of its 5% target of ETH's circulating supply.

BitMine has said it will stop purchasing ETH after hitting its target.

While BitMine accumulated, investors in US spot ETH exchange-traded funds (ETFs) divested. The products recorded $314 million in net outflows last week, their eighth consecutive week in the red.

US Spot ETH ETFs. Source: SoSoValue

Persistent inflation and rising expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will raise interest rates at its December meeting continue to weigh on Ethereum and the wider crypto market. Odds of a 25-basis-point rate hike in September surged to 99% on Monday, before easing slightly to 96%, per the CME FedWatch Tool.

Ethereum technical outlook: ETH sees rejection near $1,827

Ethereum saw a rejection just above the $1,827 resistance after a brief spike. Above that level is the 20-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) at $1,910, followed by resistance at $1,971.

data.title: HPE Stock Jumps 17% As Server Price Hikes Lift Sentiment Ahead Of Results
data.description:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) shares surged 17% on Monday after reports that server manufacturers were raising prices to offset higher memory chip costs, boosting sentiment towards companies supplying artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The Financial Times reported on Sunday that companies selling data centre equipment, including Nvidia-powered AI servers, were significantly increasing prices to pass on rising memory costs to customers.

In some cases, the increases were as high as 45%, the report said.

The news also lifted other server manufacturers. Dell Technologies (DELL) shares gained 22%, while Super Micro Computer (SMCI) rose 14%.

HPE sells enterprise technology solutions, including servers, storage systems, networking equipment and cloud services.

The company is considered a beneficiary of the growing demand for AI infrastructure.

The stock reached an all-time high in early October but subsequently fell sharply amid a broader selloff in AI-linked shares.

Despite remaining up more than 100% this year, HPE had lost nearly half its value from its October peak as investors reassessed the outlook for AI hardware companies.

HPE earnings in focus as analysts expect record revenue growth

HPE is scheduled to report its fiscal fourth-quarter results after the market closes on Monday.

Analysts expect revenue to increase 49% year over year to $14.43 billion, representing the company's highest growth rate on record.

Adjusted earnings are forecast to more than double to $1.29 per share.

The expected growth reflects an acceleration in the company's Cloud & AI business.

Management previously guided for Cloud & AI revenue growth of 60% to 72% in the fourth quarter, compared with 25% in the third quarter.

Two factors are expected to support that performance: a record $6.8 billion backlog for AI systems and a $3.5 billion inferencing deal with a hyperscaler.

The deal was signed after the third quarter ended and involves traditional servers for the customer's internal use.

The agreement highlights demand for infrastructure used to run AI models, rather than only train them.

However, hyperscaler contracts generally carry thinner margins than enterprise business.

HPE management has indicated that operating margins are likely to moderate sequentially to a mid-teens rate.

HPE price targets and server demand remain in focus

Analysts have continued to raise their estimates despite the recent weakness in HPE shares.

Last week, UBS (UBS) lowered its price target to $52 from $66 while maintaining a Neutral rating.

The firm nevertheless identified networking and server pricing as potential sources of upside in October.

According to Koyfin, 15 of the 24 analysts covering HPE rate the stock Buy or higher, while the remaining nine have Hold ratings.

Their average price target of $70.58 represents a potential upside of 73% from Friday's closing price.

The broader market environment has weighed on AI hardware stocks in recent weeks.

Concerns include rising memory costs, discussions around data centre moratoriums, midterm election results and questions about the sustainability of AI spending.

The latest reports of server price increases could provide some support to HPE and its peers, as manufacturers seek to protect their margins from higher component costs.

However, investors will be looking to Monday's results for evidence that strong demand is translating into revenue growth while the company manages its profitability.

data.title: Small Business Bankruptcies Surge Due To Strain Of Inflation And Higher Interest Rates
data.description:
Pressured by inflation and elevated borrowing costs, small businesses are going bankrupt at an accelerating rate.

Small business bankruptcy filings under Subchapter V, a fast-track process for smaller firms, surged by 46 percent through the first nine months of 2026, according to Epiq AACER.

Epiq analysts identified 469,719 total bankruptcy filings through Sept. 30, an 11 percent increase from the same period in 2025. 

Epiq AACER VP Michael Hunter said he expects bankruptcy filings to continue increasing into next year. 

"The continued increase in bankruptcy filings reflects the strain of higher borrowing costs, rising household expenses, growing consumer delinquencies, and a softer job market. As cost pressures mount, more small businesses are turning to Subchapter V to reorganize.” 

American Bankruptcy Institute executive director Amy Quackenboss noted that Congress recently passed legislation that would permanently increase the eligibility limits for both Subchapter V and Chapter 13. If President Trump signs the bill into law, it will expand access to struggling businesses and families seeking relief. 

"The increase in bankruptcy filings, especially among small businesses, highlights the challenges many debtors continue to face amid persistent inflationary pressures, elevated borrowing costs, and economic uncertainty."

Larger corporations face the same economic pressure. 

According to Cornerstone Research, large corporate filings dropped slightly in the second half of 2025 and the first half of this year. The financial consulting company identified 100 large corporate filings in the 12 months ending June 30. That was down from 117 filings in the preceding 12-month period, but still 22 percent above the annual average between 2005 and 2025. 

“The continued elevated pace of large corporate bankruptcies reflects persistent challenges of the broader economic environment for companies that rely on debt financing,” Cornerstone analyst and report author Matt Osborn said.

“The data suggest that high interest rates and regulatory uncertainty, along with shifting demand and competitive dynamics within certain sectors such as manufacturing, remain the most frequently cited drivers of distress among large bankruptcy filers.” 

Cornerstone identified higher interest rates as a source of corporate strain, saying elevated borrowing costs “weighed on companies with floating-rate debt and refinancing needs.” 

Persistent inflation was also cited as a commonly cited headwind.

This Is the Federal Reserve’s Problem

These twin headwinds expose the problem the Federal Reserve faces as it tries to combat price inflation. The central bank needs to raise rates to tackle the inflation problem. However, higher rates will raise borrowing costs even higher, increasing stress on companies that rely on debt.

This is the crux of the Fed’s Catch-22. It needs to raise and lower rates simultaneously.

Corporate debt is only a fraction of the total Debt Black Hole dominating the economy. The federal government is buried under $40.5 trillion in debt, and interest expense topped $1 trillion in the last two years. Meanwhile, American consumers are burdened by well over $1 trillion in credit card debt.

Every upward nudge to interest rates increases the power of the Debt Black Hole.

So far, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh and his minions at the Fed have taken a hawkish stance. However, if history is any indication, the central bank will ultimately choose propping up the economy with more easy money over tamping down inflation.

data.title: The Cat That Would Not Stay Dead
data.description:
On Sunday we wrote, with apologies to our feline friends, that Monday should open with a strong dead cat bounce. We now owe the cat a further apology. Nvidia's (NVDA) board announced this morning that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as president and chief executive, effective immediately. The stock is up some 34 percent from Friday’s close, hoisting the entire market behind it, led, as it nearly always is now, by AI-dominated technology. By 9:53 a.m. Central time the S&P 500 was up 5 percent. This is not a bounce. The cat has been revived to live another life.

We are not surprised that Mr. Huang is chief executive again; criminality was always unlikely. The timing is the shock. Only eleven days ago the board accepted his resignation, offered, we assume, under the threat of dismissal, and the Associated Press reports that the board had rebuffed his offer to return only days before today’s reversal. Federal and state inquiries remain open, “Yet after a brief round of meetings the directors voted unanimously to restore him, citing input from senior levels of the United States government” and their confidence that his return “poses no national security risk.”  Attorney General Todd Blanche had confirmed that the government has no evidence of unlawful conduct by Jensen Huang.

In our view, Mr. Huang grossly violated the company’s code of conduct. But a founder of his consequence to the company, and to the global economy, is a man for whom rules are apparently written in pencil. The board set its ethical concerns aside and accepted the government’s quick opinion that don’t see any criminal exposure for knowingly selling restricted chips to a Chinese shell company. Moralists may object. Markets, which are not moralists, have voted with tremendous relief.

We were looking for an inflection rebound this week, led by technology. We got a resurrection instead. This rocket-ship rally in tech this morning will stall, as such ascents do. But our 6,800 to 7,000 target zone for an S&P 500 low should now hold through the ensuing retracements, in December and again in January. CNN’s Fear and Greed Index closed Friday at an extreme reading of 10 as the S&P 500 reached ideal support, which adds to our confidence that the rally will find good footing once the near-term euphoria wears off.

Our portfolio is chasing technology and financial stocks higher this morning and will use dips to put more of our excess cash to work. Today’s news accelerates our expectation of a fourth-quarter bottom, a period during which investors can add incrementally rather than heroically.

The road ahead still has political obstacles. The first half of 2027 carries a political overhang: the prospect of fees, regulation and permitting obstacles for the AI buildout. But the AI bull market will continue.

A cat, the proverb holds, has nine lives. Nvidia has spent one of them in eleven days. Investors would be wise not to assume the supply is inexhaustible.

Unusual Stock Options Activity in WHR

WHR puts expiring Dec. 18, 2026 - Barchart Unusual Stock Options Activity Report - Nov. 23, 2026

Strong FCF Forecast

In its recent Q3 earnings report, Whirlpool reiterated a positive free cash flow (FCF) forecast for 2026. It expects to generate $300 million in FCF for the year, despite having an outflow of over $1.08 billion so far this year.

It all depends on Christmas sales. Investors can track this somewhat. Go to big-box electronics retailers and ask how well large household appliances are selling.

data.title: Nvidia Reclaims Its Trend-Line: Bottom Or Bounce?
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) reclaimed its rising trend-line today after a decisive break below it on Friday. And it did it in historic fashion, with the stock on pace for the biggest one-day gain in market value ever recorded. Even so, I’d be cautious about putting too much faith in a one-day bounce. Technically, there’s still a lot of damage to repair.

The counter argument to this though is just how many times we’ve seen V-shaped bottoms in this market, where panic selling kicks in and a rally follows almost instantly. So Nvidia is at a crossroads, and from here, both scenarios are quite plausible.

What happened to Nvidia stock?

On Friday, Nvidia dropped 14% after a report that the SEC is looking into its accounting. It closed at its lowest level of the past year, well below the rising trend-line that has supported the stock for years, and capped off its worst week since 2008.

Then this morning, Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, less than two weeks after accepting his resignation. The stock exploded higher by roughly 30%, adding over $1 trillion in market value in a single session. That’s nearly double the old record.

Why I’m cautious about a one-day bounce

A huge green candle feels great, but it doesn’t erase what happened over the last six weeks. Even after today’s rally, Nvidia is still more than 30% below its October record.

The chart also shows how much work is left. NVDA is pushing into resistance right now at the $165 level. That level was the breakout point last August and held as support this spring. Today, it’s pushing back.

Above that is the old trend-line near $175. Two weeks ago, I wrote that this same line, then sitting around $171, was the line in the sand for Nvidia. It broke, and the stock fell another 25% after that. Now it’s overhead resistance.

Beyond that, the 50-day and 200-day moving averages are both up around $205. The 50-day is rolling over hard and getting close to crossing below the 200-day.

And the SEC report hasn’t gone anywhere (though rumors it might be dropped). Huang’s return answers one question, but not that one.

Is this a V-shaped bottom for Nvidia?

Here’s the case for the bulls, and it’s a good one. Some of the most powerful rallies start exactly like this. The selling gets so extreme that everyone who wanted out is out, and then one piece of news flips the whole thing around.

Friday had a lot of the signs of capitulation: a 14% drop, the worst week since 2008, and every major chip stock in the red. Today, it reversed all at once.

There’s even history on this exact chart. The last time Nvidia tested this rising trend-line was the April 2025 selloff, and that turned into a V-shaped bottom that sent the stock to new highs. Most people didn’t believe that bounce either.

How I’d trade Nvidia from here

I’m not chasing a stock that’s up 30% in a day straight into resistance. That’s a recipe for buying the high.

For the bulls, I want to see two things. First, a close above $165, and then the $175 trend-line. Second, if the stock pulls back, I want it to hold above the rising trend-line it just reclaimed, around $145. A higher low there would go a long way toward confirming a real bottom.

For the bears, a failure back below that trend-line would be worse than the first break, because it means the reclaim didn’t stick. Friday’s lows would come right back into play.

Either way, I know exactly where I’m wrong before I put on the trade. Plan your trade, manage your risk, and the profits will take care of themselves.
